claims.claim: Engine oil pump balance shaft assembly for Toyota cars like Toyota Camry (2018–present) and Toyota RAV4
claims.evidence: Photos do not show a readable Toyota part number, engine code, or compatibility markings to confirm fitment.
No documents (invoice, shipping label) or markings indicating Belgium origin are visible.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened
claims.evidence: No test video, bench test report, or seal/fastener evidence is shown to prove it was tested or never opened.

risks.risk: Wrong part / wrong engine variant (balance shaft assemblies differ by engine code and production year). Photos don’t show the exact part number.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped/engraved part number label on the casing (and/or the Toyota OEM number) plus the engine code from the donor car (e.g., on the engine bay/engine cover).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially incompatible (worst case: buyer may not be able to fit it).

risks.risk: Condition not as claimed (may be used, worn bearings, or internal damage not visible externally).
risks.proof: Short video of the assembly running/bench-tested (showing oil pressure/rotation) or a mechanic’s test sheet with readings.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: treat as needing inspection/possible replacement).

risks.risk: Leakage or seal failure (oil pump/balance shaft assemblies can leak at seals/gaskets; not confirmable from these photos).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all seal faces/gaskets and any weep marks, plus a wipe-clean test showing no fresh oil after a short run.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as may leak (worst case: assume seals may need replacement).

risks.risk: “Never opened” claim may be false (fasteners/seals could have been disturbed; not verifiable here).
risks.proof: Photos of tamper evidence: sealant lines, factory paint marks over bolts, and any tamper tags; plus close-ups of bolt heads and gasket edges.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as possibly opened/previously serviced (worst case: unknown internal wear).

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the exact stamped/engraved OEM part number on the casing (and any Toyota logo/markings).
Photo of the engine code/vehicle details from which it was removed (donor Camry/RAV4 year + engine code).
Video or written proof of bench testing (show rotation/no abnormal noise; ideally oil pressure/flow readings).
Photos of seal faces/gaskets and any evidence of leaks, plus a short post-test wipe check.
response.reason: The photos show a metal engine oil pump/balance shaft-type assembly, but there is no readable part number or compatibility marking, and the key claims (tested working, low mileage, never opened, Belgium origin) are not provable remotely. Without the exact OEM/engine-code match, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
